description: These are the default parameters used in the reference implementation. Participants can tune these to improve performance.

morse_depth_AB.description: Morse potential depth for A-B (type 2-3) interaction
morse_depth_AB.physical_meaning: Binding strength between unsatisfied clause and catalyst
morse_depth_AB.tuning_hint: Increase to favor A-B contacts (more flip opportunities), decrease if too sticky

morse_depth_BC.description: Morse potential depth for B-C (type 3-4) interaction
morse_depth_BC.physical_meaning: Binding strength between satisfied clause and catalyst
morse_depth_BC.tuning_hint: If D_BC < D_AB, C's will unbind faster, allowing B to find new A's

morse_alpha.physical_meaning: How sharply attraction falls off with distance
morse_alpha.tuning_hint: Higher = sharper cutoff, lower = longer-range attraction

morse_r0.physical_meaning: Preferred binding distance (0 = patches can overlap)
morse_r0.tuning_hint: Keep at 0 unless you want steric constraints

contact_cutoff.description: Distance threshold for detecting patch contacts
contact_cutoff.physical_meaning: How close patches must be to trigger state change

system_parameters_readonly.comment: These cannot be changed (fixed by problem definition)

maximize_encounters.description: Increase flip opportunities by making A-B binding stronger

prevent_sticking.description: Reduce long-lived A-B or C-B bonds to increase turnover
